introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - Advanced Level Examination. Information & Communication Technologies, Subject code 0796, Paper 3 Group 1. Examination date: June 2023. Duration: two hours.**

Enter the information required in the shaded boxes. Do not write in pencil. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answer. Your results must be recorded in the spaces provided in this question booklet. Candidates must allow for themselves enough time to complete and check their work where these are required. The supervisor will guide you on how to save your files but usually you will be expected to save all your work in one folder named *Candidate folder* that will be created in your desktop. When an imperative programming language is required to write program code, either Standard [ISO] Pascal or [ANSI] C programming language may be used. You should ensure all your work is collected and printed before leaving the examination room. All printed work should be inserted in this booklet and well stapled. Carefully handle all equipment put at your disposal to avoid accidents that may lead to a disaster or system failure. Report any case of system or device malfunction to your supervisor.

**Answer ALL TASKS.**

The paper has three tasks: Task 1 (Presentation, 17 marks), Task 2 (Spreadsheet, 25 marks) and Task 3 (Programming, 7 marks).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Type a formula in cell I3 to calculate the number of matches played. Copy this formula to compute the same for other clubs. Write down the formula you have in the following cell.

I9: ........................ *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
A match was played on a day when the cell contains a result (W, D or L); an empty cell means no match. So the number of matches played by a club is the number of non-empty cells in its row from B to H.

- In **I3** type: `=COUNTA(B3:H3)` and press Enter.
- Copy I3 down to I13 (fill handle: drag the small square at the bottom right corner of the cell). The relative reference moves down with the row.

**Formula in I9:** `=COUNTA(B9:H9)` (club H, row 9). Result: **7**.

(An equivalent formula that counts only real results is `=COUNTIF(B3:H3,"W")+COUNTIF(B3:H3,"D")+COUNTIF(B3:H3,"L")`; in I9 it reads `=COUNTIF(B9:H9,"W")+COUNTIF(B9:H9,"D")+COUNTIF(B9:H9,"L")`.)

Check with the printed table: the formula gives 6, 6, 6, 7, 6, 5, 7, 6, 5, 6, 6 for clubs A, B, C, D, E, F, H, I, J, K, L, i.e. the printed column I, and the total `=SUM(I3:I13)` is 66.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Insert a formula in cell J3 to compute the number of matches won. Copy this formula to compute the same for other clubs. Write down the formula you have in the following cell.

J3: ........................ *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
A match won is represented by the letter W, so the formula counts the W in the row of the club.

**Formula in J3:** `=COUNTIF(B3:H3,"W")`

Copy J3 down to J13 (fill handle); for example J9 becomes `=COUNTIF(B9:H9,"W")`. The criterion `"W"` is written between quotation marks because it is text. The result for club A is **3**; the column gives 3, 5, 2, 1, 3, 2, 4, 1, 3, 2, 3 for clubs A, B, C, D, E, F, H, I, J, K, L, as printed, and `=SUM(J3:J13)` is 29.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Insert a formula in cell K3 to compute the number of matches drawn. Copy this formula to compute the same for other clubs. Write down the formula you have in the following cell.

K6: ........................ *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
A drawn match is represented by the letter D: the formula counts the D in the row of the club.

- In **K3** type: `=COUNTIF(B3:H3,"D")` then copy it down to K13 (fill handle).

**Formula in K6:** `=COUNTIF(B6:H6,"D")` (club D, row 6). Result: **4** (Day 2, Day 4, Day 5 and Day 7), as printed.

Remark: with the letters printed in the picture, the formula gives 2 for club A (K3) and 1 for club E (K7), where the printed column K shows 1 and 0 (the printed picture is not fully consistent on these two rows: in both rows the D of Day 3 is printed but not counted); for the other clubs the results are those printed (1, 3, 4, 2, 3, 3, 1, 3, 3). The answer expected is the formula itself, which does not change.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Type a conditional formula in B18 that will show the points scored by each club per match given that a win (W) is 3 points, draw (D) is 1 point, and a loss (L) is 0 point. Copy this formula to compute the same for other days in all the clubs. Write down the formula you have in the following cells.

B18: ........................

G23: ........................ *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The score of a match is read from the corresponding cell of the first table: the result of club A on Day 1 is in B3, and B18 is the cell for the same club and the same day in the second table (the second table is 15 rows lower). A nested IF function converts the letter:

**Formula in B18:** `=IF(B3="W",3,IF(B3="D",1,0))`

If the cell is W the result is 3; otherwise the second IF tests for D (result 1); otherwise (L or an empty cell) the result is 0. Copy B18 to the right to H18, then select B18:H18 and copy it down to row 28. All the references are relative, so each cell refers to the same position in the first table.

**Formula in G23:** `=IF(G8="W",3,IF(G8="D",1,0))`. G23 is the cell for club F (row 8) on Day 6; that cell is empty, so the result is **0**, as printed.

(Some versions of the software, for example a French-language installation, use a semicolon instead of a comma between the arguments.)

Check: the formula reproduces the printed second table for all clubs except two cells: with the letters printed in Table 1, D18 (club A, Day 3) and D22 (club E, Day 3) give 1, where the printed table shows 0.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Calculate the total scored points scored by each team. Write down the formula you have in the following cells.

I25: ........................ *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The total scored points of a club is the sum of its scored points over the 7 days.

- In **I18** type: `=SUM(B18:H18)` and copy it down to I28 (fill handle).

**Formula in I25:** `=SUM(B25:H25)` (club I). Result: 3 + 1 + 0 + 0 + 1 + 0 + 1 = **6**, as printed.

Applied to the printed Table 2, the same formula gives 10, 16, 9, 7, 9, 8, 15, 6, 10, 9, 12 for clubs A, B, C, D, E, F, H, I, J, K, L (the printed column I); the sum of the column is 111.
